text: Hunting the concurrency bug — gathering the incident and code.

result.incident: Some households have a negative combined balance, which our rules forbid. Each withdrawal checks the household's combined balance and locks the account it debits.

text: I've pinpointed the household overdraft race — now crafting proof before the fix.

result.example_violation: household combined balance negative: -100 after concurrent withdrawals (both debited, rule requires >= 0)

text: Proof confirmed — now building a fix that protects the household without slowing others.

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

args.fix: Lock both household accounts (ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE) before checking the combined balance, so concurrent withdrawals from the same household serialize while different households still run in parallel.
args.root_cause: withdraw() locked only the debited account row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on one id) then read SUM(balance) over the household without locking the partner account. Two concurrent withdrawals against the two different accounts of the same household both read the same pre-debit combined balance, both passed the check, and both debited, driving the household negative.

text: Fix accepted. Root cause: `withdraw` locked only the single debited account (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on one id) then read the household `SUM(balance)` without locking the partner row, so two concurrent withdrawals on the two accounts of one household both passed the combined-balance check and both debited. Fix locks both household rows in id order before the check.
